classification.difficultyReason: Use reference angles and quadrants, then select coterminal solutions in a negative-to-positive domain; two parts require rounding to minutes.

content.prompt: Solve each equation in the domain $[-180^\circ,180^\circ]$. Give solutions to the nearest minute where necessary.

answer.worked:
Reference angle: $\alpha=\sin^{-1}(\frac12)=30^\circ$.

Sine is positive in Q1 and Q2.

$$\begin{align*}\theta&=30^\circ,\ 180^\circ-30^\circ\\\theta&=30^\circ,150^\circ\end{align*}$$
Both solutions lie in the domain.

Reference angle: $\alpha=\tan^{-1}(1)=45^\circ$.

Tangent is positive in Q1 and Q3, giving $45^\circ$ and $225^\circ$ in $[0^\circ,360^\circ)$.

$$\begin{align*}225^\circ-360^\circ&=-135^\circ\\\theta&=45^\circ,-135^\circ\end{align*}$$

Reference angle: $\alpha=\tan^{-1}(\frac1{\sqrt3})=30^\circ$.

Tangent is negative in Q2 and Q4, giving $150^\circ$ and $330^\circ$ in $[0^\circ,360^\circ)$.

$$\begin{align*}330^\circ-360^\circ&=-30^\circ\\\theta&=150^\circ,-30^\circ\end{align*}$$

Reference angle: $\alpha=\cos^{-1}(\frac{\sqrt3}{2})=30^\circ$.

Cosine is negative in Q2 and Q3, giving $150^\circ$ and $210^\circ$ in $[0^\circ,360^\circ)$.

$$\begin{align*}210^\circ-360^\circ&=-150^\circ\\\theta&=150^\circ,-150^\circ\end{align*}$$

Let $\alpha=\tan^{-1}(0.3)$, retaining the calculator value.

Tangent is negative in Q2 and Q4. The solutions in $[0^\circ,360^\circ)$ are $180^\circ-\alpha$ and $360^\circ-\alpha$.

Subtracting $360^\circ$ from the Q4 solution gives $-\alpha$.

$$\begin{align*}-\alpha&\approx-16^\circ42'\\180^\circ-\alpha&\approx163^\circ18'\end{align*}$$
Thus $\theta=-16^\circ42',163^\circ18'$ to the nearest minute.

Cosine is zero at $90^\circ$ and $270^\circ$ in $[0^\circ,360^\circ)$.

$$\begin{align*}270^\circ-360^\circ&=-90^\circ\\x&=90^\circ,-90^\circ\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\cos\theta&=\frac1{\sqrt2}\\\alpha&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac1{\sqrt2}\right)\\\alpha&=45^\circ\end{align*}$$
Cosine is positive in Q1 and Q4, giving $45^\circ$ and $315^\circ$ in $[0^\circ,360^\circ)$.

$$\begin{align*}315^\circ-360^\circ&=-45^\circ\\\theta&=45^\circ,-45^\circ\end{align*}$$

Let $\alpha=\sin^{-1}(0.7)$, retaining the calculator value.

Sine is negative in Q3 and Q4. The solutions in $[0^\circ,360^\circ)$ are $180^\circ+\alpha$ and $360^\circ-\alpha$.

Subtract $360^\circ$ from both:

$$\begin{align*}\theta&=\alpha-180^\circ,-\alpha\\\alpha-180^\circ&\approx-135^\circ34'\\-\alpha&\approx-44^\circ26'\end{align*}$$
Thus $\theta=-135^\circ34',-44^\circ26'$ to the nearest minute.
